From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>

Elena — thanks for the clear asks. I put together three options below and attached a short proposal + cost matrix (see attachments). High level: we recommend starting with a small pilot pool and a staged reserved lane for GA to keep unit economics predictable while preserving burst capacity for launch.

Attachment stubs:
- 20280523-novamedrix-proposal.pdf (proposal + diagrams)
- novamedrix-cost-matrix.xlsx (per-hour and monthly estimates by GPU type)

Option 1 — Pilot Pool (low friction)
- Configuration: 8 x A100 (40GB) reserved for 8 weeks; network ingress + prefix caching enabled.
- Purpose: validate peak QPS, prompt patterns, KV cache hit-rate.
- Activation: immediate; refundable credits on upgrade to committed plan.
- Cost posture: lowest short-term commitment.

Option 2 — Committed Reserve (predictable pricing)
- Configuration: 32 x H100 (80GB) reserved capacity; minimum guaranteed activation: 16 GPUs (50% of the pool) for the term.
- Term: 12 months recommended.
- Ramp: initial 30 days to bring 16 GPUs online, additional 30-day windows to add +8 GPUs until reaching full 32.
- Burst: configurable burst allowance up to 50% for up to 14 days per quarter, subject to fleet availability.
- SLA & support: 99.9% uptime SLA, priority capacity routing, dedicated support lead.

Option 3 — Staged Reserved Lanes (phased on-ramp)
- Configuration: Start 12 x A100 -> month 2 add 12 x A100 -> month 4 transition 20 GPUs to H100/quantized variants as workload matures.
- Minimum guarantee: 12 GPUs active at any time.
- Flexibility: 3-stage financial cadence with mid-term true-up based on usage.
- Use case: teams that want lower near-term spend but predictable mid-term economics.

Technical notes / tradeoffs:
- GPU selection: H100s improve throughput/latency for long-context models; A100s are cost-efficient for shorter sequences. We can mix families in the same reservation for cost/perf tradeoffs.
- Caching & batching: recommend prefix caching and a 40–60ms batching window for high-throughput endpoints to reduce token cost while keeping tail latency within SLOs.
- Fallbacks: policy to fall back to hosted Redwood-verified small model variants automatically if requested capacity exceeds reserved+burst.

Next steps:
1) Quick call with Ben (sales) and Marcus (solutions) to align on commercial terms — I cc'd Ben.
2) I'm happy to convert Option 2 into a formal SOW if you prefer a committed path.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Tessa / Marcus —

Quick pricing + ops guidance below based on current Redwood Dedicated T&Cs and inventory plans. Numbers are illustrative; I'll push final banding once procurement confirms target term.

Commercial recommendation (for Option 2 — Committed Reserve):
- List: 32 x H100 (monthly amortized)
- Recommended minimum-guarantee: 12 GPUs active (this balances startup risk and ability to honor SLA).
- Discounts: 12-month term ~15% off list; 24-month ~22%; 36-month ~28% (higher for upfront payment).
- Activation window: allow 30 days to bring min-guarantee online; subsequent +8 GPU adds with 30-day notice.
- Downgrade clause: after 6 months, 1-time true-down up to 20% of committed capacity with 60 days notice (to provide flexibility).

Operational notes (Marcus please confirm):
- Burst allowance: we can commit to 50% burst for 14 days/quarter by leveraging cross-customer spare pool, with capacity fallback rules.
- Mixed GPU families: ledger will track a "compute-equivalent" metric; finance uses H100-equivalent hours for billing when families mix.
- Pre-warm KV/cache: we recommend pre-warming 25% of the KV slots 48 hours before major launch events to reduce tail latencies.

If NovaMedrix wants the staged path (Option 3), suggest: 12 A100 -> add 12 A100 at month 2 -> convert 20 GPUs to H100 in month 4. Provide a 2-line pricing delta per month for the conversion.

I'll draft the pricing bands and SOW language; Tessa, if you want, I can join the procurement call on Thursday local time.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
